name: Mahi-mahi
tile_uses: The weekend meal, tacos, rice bowls
why_now: Mahi-mahi — dorado — is a warm-water fish, and in a warm year it runs off San Diego in late summer and into the fall. It's firm, mild, and sold at most fish counters, often previously frozen. Either way, this is the month it belongs to.
how_to_choose: Moist and glossy, with no gaps between the layers
It should smell like the ocean, nothing else
buy_this_much: 1½ lbs. The weekend meal, plus tacos or a rice bowl the next day.
price_note: Previously frozen mahi is often as good as fresh and usually cheaper. If the counter is out, any firm white fillet works.

flavor_paths.name: Chile-rubbed
flavor_paths.description: Painted with roasted chile paste, charred in a hot pan. The weekend meal.

flavor_paths.name: Green
flavor_paths.description: Flaked into tortillas with salsa verde.

flavor_paths.name: Pickled
flavor_paths.description: Over rice with escabeche and its brine.

weekday_uses: Flaked into tacos with salsa verde
Over a rice bowl with escabeche
Cold, the next day, with lime and salt
weekend_use: Chile-rubbed, charred, and flaked into warm tortillas. The weekend meal.
storage: Cook it the day you buy it, or the next. Thaw previously frozen fish in the fridge, not on the counter.
one_thing_to_learn: Firm fish like mahi can take a marinade or a paste; delicate fish like sole can't. The firmer the flesh, the more seasoning it can carry and the hotter the pan it can handle.
market_question: Was this frozen, and when did it come in?
